answer.rationale: The finance mandate and expiring contract create pressure to switch to the low-cost vendor (memory_c2), but that memory only documents cost and invoicing outcomes—it says nothing about delivery reliability, and the assembly line has zero volume buffer, making any switch a high delivery-risk move to verify before acting on. I verified memory_c2's source to check for any omitted reliability signal; absent stronger evidence there, I'm not switching primary vendor this cycle. Instead, negotiate_terms with the incumbent leverages memory_c4 (benchmarking recovered margin at renewal) and memory_c6 (multi-year volume commitments cut unit cost without narrowing service scope) to pursue meaningful cost reduction toward the 18% target while preserving the delivery stability documented in memory_c1. This keeps TCO improving without introducing untested supply risk during a zero-buffer period. Switching vendors or adding a second source remains viable for the next review cycle once the low-cost vendor's reliability under full-volume commitment can be verified.
